title: Runtime Profile Observability – Dashboard & Alert Spec (Profile Pack v1)
author: Allison Grant
body:
## Purpose
This page specifies the dashboards and alerting required to safely operate Redwood’s **hardware tuning profiles pack** (runtime kernel + scheduling + KV/memory defaults) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals:
- Make profile behavior **comparable** across SKUs (H100, L40S, B200) and across profile versions.
- Provide fast triage signals for performance regressions: **queueing**, **kernel fallbacks**, **KV cache efficiency**, **fragmentation**, and **OOM/near-OOM**.
- Define a minimal, stable set of **metric names + tags** so perf-canary, benchmark-lab, and SRE runbooks align.

Non-goals:
- This spec is not a full SLO policy doc (see rollout guardrails page). It focuses on **instrumentation, dashboards, and alert thresholds**.

---

## Audience
- Runtime owners (kernel/scheduler/KV): confirm expected behavior and debug regressions.
- SRE/on-call: detect and mitigate incidents during profile rollouts.
- Infra: correlate behavior with fleet heterogeneity (driver/CUDA, PCIe vs SXM, MIG).

---

## Dashboard inventory
### 1) Dashboard: “Runtime Profiles – Overview” (primary)
**Use cases:**
- “What profile(s) are active right now by SKU/region?”
- “Did p95/p99 latency change after default profile_version moved?”
- “Are we seeing kernel fallback or queue buildup correlated with one profile_id?”

**Required filters (top-of-dashboard variables):**
- env: {prod, staging}
- deployment_mode: {hosted, dedicated, private}
- region
- sku
- model_family
- profile_version
- profile_id

### 2) Dashboard: “Runtime Profiles – Deep Dive (per route/model)” (secondary)
**Use cases:**
- Debug a single model/endpoint experiencing tail latency.
- Validate a canary cohort vs baseline with identical traffic shape.

**Required filters:**
- route (or endpoint_id)
- model
- tenant_id (Dedicated only; restricted visibility)
- pool / gpu_cluster

### 3) Dashboard: “Runtime Profiles – Memory/KV & Stability” (secondary)
**Use cases:**
- Identify fragmentation-driven p99 and OOM risk.
- Confirm KV cache headroom and compaction behavior matches expected behavior docs.

---

## Metrics & naming
### Conventions
- Metrics are emitted from serving runtime (and runtime sidecars where applicable).
- Naming is Prometheus-style (snake_case). Equivalent Datadog naming can be derived by ingestion rules; do not fork semantics.
- All latency histograms must support percentile queries at p50/p95/p99.

### Required tags/labels (low cardinality)
All metrics in this spec MUST include these tags whenever known:
- env
- deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)
- region
- sku (h100|l40s|b200 + optional suffix for form factor if stable, e.g., h100_sxm vs h100_pcie)
- driver_major (e.g., 550)
- cuda_major (e.g., 12)
- runtime_version (e.g., 1.22.0)
- profile_version (e.g., 1.0.0)
- profile_id (e.g., h100_default_v3_attention_sched_v2)
- model_family (e.g., llama, qwen, mistral; keep to curated set)

### Optional tags (use carefully)
Allowed on select metrics only (see cardinality guidance):
- model (full model id) – allowed only on per-model deep dive dashboards.
- route/endpoint_id – allowed only on request-level latency/volume metrics.
- kernel_variant (e.g., attn_v2, attn_v3) – allowed only on kernel choice/fallback metrics.
- workload_bucket (short enum; see below).

### High-cardinality tags (disallowed by default)
Do NOT add these tags to global histograms/counters:
- request_id, prompt_hash, user_id
- full driver/cuda patch version strings
- raw sequence_length

---

## Workload buckets (standard enums)
All queueing and scheduler metrics should include workload_bucket:
- short: prompt <= 256 and expected_decode <= 128
- medium: prompt 257–2048 or expected_decode 129–512
- long_context: prompt > 2048
- long_decode: expected_decode > 512
- mixed_unknown: missing predictors or mixed batch composition

Note: “expected_decode” should be derived from request parameters (max_tokens) or route policy, not from realized tokens.

---

## Metric catalog (required)
### A) Traffic & health
1) runtime_requests_total (counter)
- Definition: number of requests admitted for execution.
- Tags: required + route (allowed), model_family.

2) runtime_request_rejects_total (counter)
- Definition: admission control rejects due to queue/memory headroom limits.
- Tags: required + reason (enum: queue_full|oom_risk|profile_incompatible|capacity_guardrail).

3) runtime_errors_total (counter)
- Definition: request failures after admission.
- Tags: required + error_class (enum: oom|cuda|timeout|internal|canceled).

### B) End-to-end latency and stage breakdown
4) runtime_request_latency_ms (histogram)
- Definition: end-to-end request latency (including queueing).
- Tags: required + route (allowed), workload_bucket.

5) runtime_queue_ms (histogram)
- Definition: time from admission to start of GPU compute.
- Tags: required + workload_bucket.

6) runtime_compute_ms (histogram)
- Definition: total time spent in GPU compute for request.
- Tags: required + workload_bucket.

7) runtime_prefill_ms (histogram)
- Definition: prefill stage latency.
- Tags: required + workload_bucket.

8) runtime_decode_ms (histogram)
- Definition: decode stage latency (aggregate).
- Tags: required + workload_bucket.

9) runtime_tokens_generated_total (counter)
- Definition: total generated tokens.
- Tags: required + route (allowed), workload_bucket.

10) runtime_tokens_per_sec (gauge or derived)
- Definition: tokens/sec at worker or pool scope.
- Implementation: can be derived from tokens_generated_total and time; do not emit per-request.
- Tags: required.

### C) Scheduler & batching
11) scheduler_active_batches (gauge)
- Definition: number of batches currently executing.
- Tags: required.

12) scheduler_batch_size (histogram)
- Definition: realized batch size distribution.
- Tags: required + workload_bucket.

13) scheduler_queue_depth (gauge)
- Definition: number of requests waiting in scheduler queue.
- Tags: required + workload_bucket.

14) scheduler_preemptions_total (counter)
- Definition: number of times a request was preempted/backpressured (if supported).
- Tags: required + reason (enum: fairness|memory_pressure|tail_latency_guardrail).

### D) Kernel selection & fallback
15) kernel_choice_total (counter)
- Definition: chosen kernel variant per major op (attention) at runtime.
- Tags: required + op (enum: attention|gemm|rope) + kernel_variant.

16) kernel_fallback_total (counter)
- Definition: kernel fallback events where preferred variant was not used.
- Tags: required + op + from_variant + to_variant + reason.
- reason enum (keep stable): unsupported_shape|driver_incompat|cuda_incompat|oom_risk|numerics_guard|unknown.

17) kernel_fallback_rate (derived)
- Definition: kernel_fallback_total / kernel_choice_total by op.
- Used for alerting and rollout gates.

### E) KV cache & caching efficiency
18) kv_cache_hit_rate (gauge)
- Definition: fraction of requests/tokens served with KV/prefix reuse where eligible.
- Tags: required + cache_type (enum: prefix|kv).

19) kv_cache_evictions_total (counter)
- Definition: evictions due to capacity or policy.
- Tags: required + reason (enum: capacity|ttl|fragmentation|policy).

20) kv_cache_bytes (gauge)
- Definition: bytes allocated for KV cache.
- Tags: required.

21) kv_cache_compactions_total (counter)
- Definition: number of compaction events.
- Tags: required.

22) kv_cache_compaction_ms (histogram)
- Definition: time spent in compaction.
- Tags: required.

### F) Memory, fragmentation, and OOM risk
23) gpu_memory_allocated_bytes (gauge)
- Definition: allocated GPU memory observed by runtime allocator.
- Tags: required.

24) gpu_memory_reserved_bytes (gauge)
- Definition: reserved/managed GPU memory (allocator reservation).
- Tags: required.

25) gpu_memory_free_bytes (gauge)
- Definition: estimated free memory.
- Tags: required.

26) memory_fragmentation_ratio (gauge)
- Definition: allocator fragmentation estimate; 0 = ideal, higher = worse.
- Tags: required.

27) memory_allocation_failures_total (counter)
- Definition: allocation failures that may precede OOM.
- Tags: required.

28) runtime_oom_events_total (counter)
- Definition: OOM events (CUDA OOM or allocator OOM).
- Tags: required + stage (enum: prefill|decode|load|other).

29) runtime_near_oom_total (counter)
- Definition: headroom guard triggered (request refused or forced fallback due to low headroom).
- Tags: required + action (enum: reject|fallback|shrink_kv|reduce_concurrency).

---

## Dashboard panels (minimum required)
### Runtime Profiles – Overview (must-have panels)
1) Profile adoption
- Panel: stacked area of runtime_requests_total by profile_version + sku.
- Panel: table of top profile_id by request volume (last 1h, 24h).

2) Latency by profile
- Panel: p95/p99 runtime_request_latency_ms by profile_version (split by sku).
- Panel: p95 runtime_queue_ms by profile_version (split by workload_bucket).

3) Stage breakdown
- Panel: p95 runtime_prefill_ms and runtime_decode_ms (two lines) by profile_id.
- Panel: p95 runtime_compute_ms vs runtime_queue_ms ratio (detect queue-driven regressions).

4) Scheduler health
- Panel: scheduler_queue_depth p95 and max by sku.
- Panel: scheduler_batch_size distribution (heatmap or histogram over time).
- Panel: runtime_request_rejects_total by reason.

5) Kernel fallback
- Panel: kernel_fallback_rate by op (attention primary) and sku.
- Panel: kernel_fallback_total by reason (top reasons over 1h).

6) KV cache
- Panel: kv_cache_hit_rate by cache_type and sku.
- Panel: kv_cache_compactions_total and kv_cache_compaction_ms p95.

7) Memory stability
- Panel: gpu_memory_allocated_bytes and gpu_memory_free_bytes (same chart) by sku.
- Panel: memory_fragmentation_ratio p95 by profile_id.
- Panel: runtime_near_oom_total and runtime_oom_events_total (rate).

### Runtime Profiles – Deep Dive (recommended panels)
- Top routes/models by p99 latency (restricted in Dedicated if tenant scoping is required).
- Correlation view: p99 latency vs kernel_fallback_rate vs queue_ms.
- Compare canary cohort vs baseline cohort (requires cohort tag; see rollout).

### Runtime Profiles – Memory/KV & Stability (recommended panels)
- Fragmentation ratio vs compaction time vs near-OOM.
- KV cache bytes vs hit rate vs evictions.
- OOM events by stage (prefill vs decode) and by sku.

---

## Alerting spec
### Alert routing policy
- Paging (PagerDuty): signals that indicate imminent or active user impact.
- Slack-only warning: early indicators during rollout or bring-up.
- Ticket (Jira): longer-term drift or capacity hygiene issues.

Owner rotations:
- Primary: SRE on-call
- Secondary: Runtime on-call (kernel/scheduler)

### Rollout-critical alerts (page)
1) Tail latency regression correlated with profile
- Condition: p99 runtime_request_latency_ms increases > 20% vs trailing 24h baseline for same sku + region + model_family, sustained 10 minutes.
- Scope: hosted canary cohorts first; expand to prod.
- Tags: sku, region, profile_version, model_family.
- Action: trigger kill-switch / rollback to previous default profile_version per rollout runbook.

2) Queueing surge (likely saturation or scheduler bug)
- Condition: p95 runtime_queue_ms > 150ms for H100 OR > 250ms for L40S, sustained 10 minutes, AND runtime_requests_total steady/increasing.
- Add’l gate: scheduler_queue_depth max > configured limit for 5 minutes.
- Action: reduce concurrency limits, verify admission control, evaluate recent profile change.

3) Kernel fallback spike (performance cliff risk)
- Condition: kernel_fallback_rate(op=attention) > 2% for H100 OR > 5% for L40S, sustained 15 minutes.
- Page only if correlated with latency increase (>10% p95 request latency) OR if fallback reason is driver_incompat/cuda_incompat.
- Action: confirm detected driver/cuda tags; roll back profile or adjust compatibility gates.

4) OOM events
- Condition: runtime_oom_events_total rate > 0.05/min per pool for 10 minutes OR any OOM burst > 3 events in 5 minutes.
- Action: cap concurrency / adjust KV headroom, verify profile_id; consider immediate rollback.

### Early warning alerts (Slack)
5) Near-OOM guard triggers rising
- Condition: runtime_near_oom_total increases > 3x day-over-day for a given sku/profile_id (30m window).
- Action: inspect gpu_memory_free_bytes trend and fragmentation ratio; validate headroom settings.

6) Fragmentation degradation
- Condition: memory_fragmentation_ratio p95 > 0.35 for 30 minutes for any sku/profile_id.
- Action: check compaction metrics; if compaction_ms p95 also elevated, investigate allocator knobs in profile.

7) KV cache hit rate drop
- Condition: kv_cache_hit_rate decreases > 15 percentage points vs trailing 24h baseline for same sku + model_family (30m window).
- Action: confirm no route-level cache disable; inspect evictions_total and KV bytes.

### Bring-up / B200-specific alerts (Slack -> page if persistent)
8) Compatibility gate failures
- Condition: runtime_request_rejects_total{reason=profile_incompatible} > 0 in prod.
- Action: verify SKU detection and driver/cuda baseline; ensure B200 requires explicit profile_version pin when mandated.

---

## Threshold rationale & notes
- Thresholds above are tuned to catch **profile-induced deltas** quickly without paging on normal load variation.
- All “baseline comparisons” should use like-for-like slicing: sku + region + model_family at minimum.
- For Dedicated, per-tenant paging should be disabled by default unless explicitly requested; use pool/cluster scope + customer escalation procedures.

---

## Cardinality & aggregation guidance
- Global dashboards should aggregate at (sku, region, deployment_mode, profile_version/profile_id, model_family).
- Route and model tags are allowed only in deep-dive dashboards and must be behind filters to prevent wide fan-out.
- kernel_variant tags must be limited to a small enumerated set; do not include compile-time hashes.
- workload_bucket is required and intentionally small; do not emit raw token lengths as tags.

---

## Implementation checklist (for runtime + observability)
1) Ensure runtime exports required labels: profile_id, profile_version, sku, driver_major, cuda_major.
2) Confirm histogram buckets for latency metrics are appropriate (capture 5ms–60s).
3) Add unit tests in runtime/observability-pack that validate required tags are present.
4) Add golden dashboard JSON updates in observability-pack with versioned panels.
5) Validate in staging with synthetic load and confirm:
   - profile adoption panels show both baseline and canary cohorts
   - kernel fallback reasons are non-empty and stable
   - OOM and near-OOM counters increment in induced scenarios

---
